entries.claim: The README says that with a spine there, `/seldon architecture` writes architecture.md. SKILL.md lines 58-60 (the f4394ed fix) write nothing when the brief or the PRD is missing, even with a spine on disk, so a spine alone is not enough.
entries.failure_scenario: Start with `.planning/seldon/` holding brief.md and spine.md, with prd.md deleted by hand so the user can redo it, and run `/seldon architecture`. Going by the README, the user expects architecture.md. The skill follows its 'No brief or no PRD there' route instead: it writes nothing and points to `/seldon prd`.

entries.claim: The README says the spine step 'asks what runs with nobody there', but the fixed question in SKILL.md line 777 is 'When should it run with nobody there?'. The skill finds the unattended part in the brief and PRD itself and asks only when it should run.
entries.failure_scenario: A PRD has a daily job, as in the spine-job case. A reader of the README expects to be asked which parts run unattended. Seldon names the job itself and asks only when it should run, which is the question the spine-job and spine-answers graders match.

entries.claim: The spine-from-prd line says the case checks that Seldon 'writes or edits no other file'. Its graders no-write-but-spine.md and no-edit-but-spine.md only match file paths under `.planning/seldon/` other than spine.md, and case.yaml says 'no other file in .planning/seldon/'.
entries.failure_scenario: During spine-from-prd, Seldon calls Write or Edit on a file outside `.planning/seldon/`, for example `docs/notes.md`. The input_match regex needs `.planning/seldon/` in the path, so neither grader counts the call and the case passes, even though the README says the case checks for that.
